title: Isolated Islands, Archipelagos & Coral Atolls
description: Comprehensive 60-question maritime odyssey exploring continental giants, volcanic hotspots, remote ocean outposts, and coral atolls.

questions.question: What is the largest non-continental island on Earth by surface area, covering over 2.1 million square kilometers?
questions.explanation: Greenland is an autonomous territory within the Kingdom of Denmark, covered largely by a massive permanent ice sheet.

questions.question: What is the second-largest island in the world, divided between Papua New Guinea and Indonesia?
questions.explanation: New Guinea covers roughly 785,753 square kilometers and is renowned for extreme biological diversity and linguistic variety.

questions.question: Which Southeast Asian island is the third-largest on Earth and the only island shared by three sovereign nations?
questions.explanation: Borneo is divided among Indonesia Kalimantan, the Malaysian states of Sabah and Sarawak, and the sovereign Sultanate of Brunei.

questions.question: What island off the southeastern coast of Africa is the fourth-largest island on Earth, isolated for over eighty million years?
questions.explanation: Madagascar split from the Indian landmass millions of years ago, evolving unique wildlife such as lemurs and baobab trees.

questions.question: What is the largest island in Canada and the fifth-largest island in the world, located in the northern territory of Nunavut?
questions.explanation: Baffin Island covers over 507,000 square kilometers, named after English navigator William Baffin who explored the Arctic waterway.

questions.question: What is the approximate total surface area in thousands of square kilometers of Greenland?
questions.explanation: Greenland encompasses roughly 2,166,086 square kilometers, making it more than three times the size of Texas.

questions.question: Which nation is the world largest archipelagic state, comprising over seventeen thousand islands across five thousand kilometers?
questions.explanation: Indonesia spans from Sumatra in the west to Papua in the east, encompassing major islands including Java, Kalimantan, and Sulawesi.

questions.question: Which Pacific island nation consists of an archipelago of over 7,600 islands categorized into Luzon, Visayas, and Mindanao?
questions.explanation: The Philippine archipelago sits along the Pacific Ring of Fire, featuring rich coral reefs and deep oceanic trenches.

questions.question: What is the largest and most populous of the four main home islands that make up the Japanese archipelago?
questions.explanation: Honshu contains Tokyo, Osaka, Kyoto, and Mount Fuji, housing over eighty percent of the total Japanese population.

questions.question: Which Indian Ocean nation comprises twenty-six natural coral atolls and has the lowest average ground elevation on Earth at 1.5 meters?
questions.explanation: The Maldives consists of nearly 1,200 coral islands dispersed across 90,000 square kilometers of equatorial Indian Ocean.

questions.question: Which archipelago nation in the western Indian Ocean is unique for containing the world only oceanic islands formed of ancient continental granite?
questions.explanation: The granitic Inner Seychelles islands are fragments of the ancient supercontinent Gondwana that remained above sea level.

questions.question: What is the officially recorded total count of registered islands making up the Indonesian archipelago?
questions.explanation: Geospatial surveys by the Indonesian government have cataloged approximately 17,508 islands, of which around 6,000 are inhabited.

questions.question: What volcanic archipelago in the South Atlantic is recognized as the most remote permanently inhabited archipelago on Earth?
questions.explanation: Tristan da Cunha lies over 2,400 kilometers from the nearest inhabited land of Saint Helena and 2,800 kilometers from South Africa.

questions.question: What isolated Polynesian volcanic island in the southeastern Pacific is famous for nearly one thousand monumental stone statues named Moai?
questions.explanation: Rapa Nui or Easter Island was settled by Polynesian voyagers who carved monolithic volcanic tuff statues between 1250 and 1500 CE.

questions.question: Which glacier-covered uninhabited volcanic island in the South Atlantic is recognized as the single most remote point of land on Earth?
questions.explanation: Bouvet Island is a Norwegian dependency located over 1,600 kilometers from Antarctica and 2,200 kilometers from Gough Island.

questions.question: Which tiny South Pacific volcanic island became the permanent refuge for the historic HMS Bounty mutineers led by Fletcher Christian in 1790?
questions.explanation: Pitcairn Island remains the smallest and least populous sovereign British Overseas Territory with roughly fifty residents.

questions.question: On which isolated British volcanic island in the South Atlantic did French Emperor Napoleon Bonaparte live in exile until his death in 1821?
questions.explanation: Napoleon was imprisoned at Longwood House on Saint Helena following his final defeat at the Battle of Waterloo in 1815.

questions.question: What is the approximate straight-line distance in kilometers from Tristan da Cunha to the nearest continental mainland in South Africa?
questions.explanation: Tristan da Cunha lies approximately 2,816 kilometers west of Cape Town, South Africa, accessible only by a six-day boat voyage.

questions.question: What is the world largest coral reef system, stretching over 2,300 kilometers off the northeastern coast of Queensland, Australia?
questions.explanation: The Great Barrier Reef comprises nearly 3,000 individual reefs and 900 islands, visible from Earth orbit.

questions.question: Which remote raised coral atoll in the Seychelles is the second-largest atoll on Earth and home to the world largest giant tortoise colony?
questions.explanation: Aldabra hosts over 100,000 endemic Aldabra giant tortoises, protected as a pristine UNESCO World Heritage natural site.

questions.question: Which coral atoll in the Marshall Islands features the largest enclosed lagoon in the world by surface area, covering over 2,170 square kilometers?
questions.explanation: Kwajalein Atoll surrounds an enormous lagoon with nearly one hundred islets, serving as a key missile testing range.

questions.question: Which Micronesian atoll in the Marshall Islands was the site of twenty-three nuclear weapons tests conducted by the United States between 1946 and 1958?
questions.explanation: Bikini Atoll was the site of Castle Bravo in 1954, the largest thermonuclear explosion ever detonated by the United States.

questions.question: What famous French Polynesian island in the Leeward Society Islands is formed of an extinct volcano surrounded by a turquoise barrier lagoon?
questions.explanation: Bora Bora is crowned by the basalt peaks of Mount Otemanu and Mount Pahia, surrounded by an outer ring of coral motus.

questions.question: What is the approximate total length in kilometers of the Great Barrier Reef along the Australian coast?
questions.explanation: The Great Barrier Reef extends approximately 2,300 kilometers along the continental shelf of Queensland.

questions.question: Which Norwegian Arctic archipelago halfway between Norway and the North Pole hosts the Global Seed Vault inside permafrost rock?
questions.explanation: The Svalbard Global Seed Vault on the island of Spitsbergen preserves millions of backup crop seed samples deep in frozen sandstone.

questions.question: On which glaciated sub-Antarctic island is legendary polar explorer Sir Ernest Shackleton buried at the former whaling station of Grytviken?
questions.explanation: Shackleton died aboard the Quest in 1922 and was laid to rest in the Grytviken cemetery on mountainous South Georgia.

questions.question: Which remote French southern territory in the southern Indian Ocean is known as the Desolation Islands due to gale winds and barren terrain?
questions.explanation: The Kerguelen archipelago is an isolated volcanic plateau populated only by French researchers, elephant seals, and king penguins.

questions.question: What is the northernmost major island in the Canadian Arctic Archipelago, separated from Greenland only by the narrow Nares Strait?
questions.explanation: Ellesmere Island hosts Cape Columbia, the northernmost point of land in Canada, and the year-round military research station Alert.

questions.question: Which Arctic archipelago belonging to Russia served as the testing ground for the Tsar Bomba, the largest nuclear detonation in human history?
questions.explanation: Novaya Zemlya is a mountainous Arctic island chain dividing the Barents and Kara seas, used as a major Soviet nuclear test range.

questions.question: In what year did the Svalbard Global Seed Vault officially open in the Norwegian Arctic?
questions.explanation: The Svalbard Global Seed Vault was officially opened on February 26, 2008, to provide permanent insurance against global agricultural loss.

questions.question: Which oceanic archipelago was formed over millions of years as the Pacific tectonic plate migrated northwest across a stationary mantle plume?
questions.explanation: The Hawaiian-Emperor seamount chain stretches over 6,000 kilometers, with active shield volcanoes Kilauea and Mauna Loa on Hawaii Island.

questions.question: Which Pacific volcanic archipelago located on the Equator inspired Charles Darwin theory of natural selection during his 1835 visit?
questions.explanation: Darwin studied the distinct adaptive beak morphologies of finches and carapaces of giant tortoises across different Galápagos islands.

questions.question: Which North Atlantic island nation sits directly astride both the divergent Mid-Atlantic Ridge and a deep thermal mantle plume?
questions.explanation: Iceland rifts apart along the North American and Eurasian plates, resulting in extensive volcanism, geysers, and geothermal energy.

questions.question: Which autonomous Spanish archipelago off the coast of northwest Africa is crowned by the 3,715-meter volcanic peak of Mount Teide?
questions.explanation: The Canary Islands comprise seven main volcanic islands including Tenerife, Gran Canaria, Lanzarote, and Fuerteventura.

questions.question: Which Portuguese volcanic archipelago in the mid-Atlantic consists of nine islands spread across three distinct tectonic groups?
questions.explanation: The Azores lie near the triple junction where the North American, Eurasian, and African tectonic plates meet.

questions.question: In what year did English naturalist Charles Darwin visit the Galápagos Islands aboard HMS Beagle?
questions.explanation: Charles Darwin arrived in the Galápagos archipelago in September 1835, collecting zoological specimens that shaped On the Origin of Species.

questions.question: What is the largest island in the Mediterranean Sea, separated from the Italian mainland by the narrow Strait of Messina?
questions.explanation: Sicily spans over 25,700 square kilometers, dominated by the active volcano Mount Etna and historic Greco-Roman temples.

questions.question: What is the largest and most populous of the Greek islands, famous for the ancient Minoan Bronze Age palace of Knossos?
questions.explanation: Crete was the center of Europe earliest advanced civilization, the Minoans, who flourished from roughly 2700 to 1420 BCE.

questions.question: Which Mediterranean island nation is geographically in Western Asia but politically integrated into the European Union?
questions.explanation: Cyprus is divided by a UN buffer zone known as the Green Line separating the Republic of Cyprus from Northern Cyprus.

questions.question: Which mountainous French Mediterranean island located north of Sardinia is celebrated as the birthplace of Napoleon Bonaparte?
questions.explanation: Napoleon was born in Ajaccio, Corsica, in 1769, shortly after the Republic of Genoa ceded the island to France.

questions.question: What is the largest island on the European continent and the ninth-largest island in the world by surface area?
questions.explanation: Great Britain covers over 209,000 square kilometers and comprises England, Scotland, and Wales.

questions.question: What is the total surface area in square kilometers of Sicily, the largest island in the Mediterranean?
questions.explanation: Sicily encompasses 25,711 square kilometers of diverse agricultural plains, coastal cliffs, and volcanic highlands.

questions.question: Which Caribbean island is shared by two sovereign nations: Haiti occupying the western third and the Dominican Republic the eastern two-thirds?
questions.explanation: Hispaniola was the site of the first permanent European settlement in the Americas founded by Christopher Columbus in 1492.

questions.question: Which European island in the North Atlantic is politically divided between the independent Republic of Ireland and Northern Ireland?
questions.explanation: The island of Ireland was partitioned in 1921 under the Government of Ireland Act, creating six northern counties within the UK.

questions.question: What small Caribbean island is divided between a northern French overseas collectivity and a southern Dutch constituent country?
questions.explanation: Saint Martin / Sint Maarten is the smallest inhabited island in the world divided between two sovereign nations, partitioned in 1648.

questions.question: Which archipelago at the southern tip of South America is divided between Chile and Argentina by the Beagle Channel and meridian lines?
questions.explanation: Isla Grande de Tierra del Fuego is partitioned with western fjords belonging to Chile and eastern plains belonging to Argentina.

questions.question: How many sovereign nations share territory on the Southeast Asian island of Borneo?
questions.explanation: Borneo is uniquely shared by three sovereign countries: Brunei, Malaysia, and Indonesia.

questions.question: How many sovereign nations have territorial sovereignty over parts of the island of Borneo?
questions.explanation: Borneo is divided among Indonesia (approx 73%), Malaysia (approx 26%), and the Sultanate of Brunei (approx 1%).

questions.question: What percentage of floral species found on the island of Madagascar are completely endemic, occurring nowhere else on Earth?
questions.explanation: Over 11,000 plant species in Madagascar are strictly endemic, including six of the world eight distinct baobab tree species.

questions.question: Which Indonesian island is the primary natural habitat of the Komodo dragon, the heaviest living lizard species on Earth?
questions.explanation: Varanus komodoensis thrives in the dry savannas of Komodo, Rinca, and Flores islands within Komodo National Park.

questions.question: Which Yemeni island in the Arabian Sea is famous for bizarre endemic flora including the umbrella-shaped Dragon Blood Tree?
questions.explanation: Socotra is described as the most alien-looking place on Earth, with one-third of its plant species found nowhere else.

questions.question: Which Australian island state south of Bass Strait is the exclusive wild habitat of the carnivorous marsupial the Tasmanian devil?
questions.explanation: Tasmania served as a natural refuge for marsupials extinct on the mainland, including the Tasmanian devil and the extinct thylacine.

questions.question: Which flightless, nocturnal ratite bird with hair-like feathers and nostrils at the tip of its beak is the national emblem of New Zealand?
questions.explanation: The kiwi evolved in the absence of native terrestrial mammalian predators on the isolated islands of New Zealand.

questions.question: What approximate percentage of the native flora of Madagascar is entirely endemic to the island?
questions.explanation: Botanists estimate that roughly ninety percent of Madagascar twelve thousand plant species grow nowhere else naturally.

questions.question: What Indonesian island is the most populous island on Earth, home to over 150 million residents and more than half the national population?
questions.explanation: Java is one of the most densely settled major islands in the world, hosting Jakarta, Surabaya, Bandung, and numerous active volcanoes.

questions.question: What island off the coast of Queensland, Australia, is recognized as the largest sand island in the world, known traditionally as K gari?
questions.explanation: K gari spans over 1,840 square kilometers of massive parabolic sand dunes, perched freshwater dune lakes, and rainforest growing in sand.

questions.question: Which volcanic island emerged from the North Atlantic Ocean near Iceland during a continuous submarine eruption from 1963 to 1967?
questions.explanation: Surtsey is a pristine natural laboratory protected from human interference to study primary biological colonization on new land.

questions.question: According to Guinness World Records, what tiny rock ledge in the Isles of Scilly holds the title of the smallest island with a building on it?
questions.explanation: Bishop Rock is capped entirely by a forty-nine-meter-tall granite Victorian lighthouse built to guide ships entering the English Channel.

questions.question: Which low-lying Pacific atoll nation comprising nine coral islands is one of the most vulnerable nations on Earth to rising sea levels?
questions.explanation: Tuvalu has a maximum elevation of less than five meters above sea level, pioneering digital nationhood initiatives.

questions.question: In what year did the volcanic island of Surtsey first emerge above sea level off the southern coast of Iceland?
questions.explanation: Surtsey broke through the ocean surface on November 14, 1963, creating an island of 2.7 square kilometers.
